title: International Trade
tagline: Patterns of trade and gravity, the Ricardian model, specific factors, Heckscher–Ohlin, increasing returns, firms and value chains, trade-policy instruments, political economy and trade agreements
summary: Why do countries trade, what do they trade, and who gains and who loses? This course develops the classical and modern theories of international trade — the Ricardian model, the specific-factors and Heckscher–Ohlin models, increasing returns and monopolistic competition, and heterogeneous firms — and uses them to analyse tariffs, quotas and subsidies, global value chains, the political economy of protection and the world trading system.

chapters.title: Patterns of world trade
chapters.summary: Who trades with whom, the gravity equation, and how trade has changed as transport and communication costs fell.

chapters.title: Comparative advantage: the Ricardian model
chapters.summary: Labour productivity, relative prices and the gains from trade when countries differ in technology.

chapters.title: Specific factors and income distribution
chapters.summary: Why trade creates winners and losers when some factors of production cannot move between industries.

chapters.title: Factor endowments: the Heckscher–Ohlin model
chapters.summary: Trade driven by differences in capital and labour, the Stolper–Samuelson and Rybczynski theorems, and the evidence.

chapters.title: Increasing returns and imperfect competition
chapters.summary: Intra-industry trade, monopolistic competition, the home-market effect and economic geography.

chapters.title: Firms in the global economy
chapters.summary: Heterogeneous firms and the Melitz model, exporting, multinational production and global value chains.

chapters.title: The instruments of trade policy
chapters.summary: Tariffs, quotas and export subsidies in partial and general equilibrium, the large-country case and the optimal tariff.

chapters.title: The political economy of trade policy
chapters.summary: Why countries protect industries: interest groups and lobbying, infant industries and strategic trade policy.

chapters.title: Trade agreements and the world trading system
chapters.summary: The GATT and the WTO, regional trade agreements, trade wars and the settlement of trade disputes.
